purpose: Use one same-canonical hourly RRULE as bounded cold rescue with a strict normal CONTINUE fast continuation of actual observed turn END + 60 seconds; predictive prearm remains evidence-gated.
canonical_invariant: Never create a replacement canonical merely to continue this actor. Mutate only the verified canonical identified by fresh durable state.

provisional_arm.when: Immediately after minimum stale-wake/fence/authority validation and before full restore or substantive work.
provisional_arm.reason: If the active turn dies before normal close, the same canonical retains a bounded cold-rescue opportunity.
provisional_arm.mutation_failure: Retry once when safe. If an older verified future continuation remains alive, enter DEGRADED_CONTINUATION and continue only within its safety envelope; otherwise fail closed before substantive side effects.

work.rule: Perform sustained useful authorized work by chaining bounded units. If a unit completes before 600 elapsed seconds, start the next clear low-risk checkpointable unit or a smaller decomposed slice. At >=600s, do not start a new large unit; close after the smallest safe in-flight boundary. Normal soft ceiling is ~720s.
work.checkpoint_rule: Persist enough durable progress that a cold successor can resume without chat context.
work.collision_rule: If useful work remains and provisional due approaches too closely, extend the provisional DTSTART before collision, then verify.

normal_final_rearm.due: actual observed turn END timestamp + exactly 60 seconds, preserving seconds exactly; minute rounding is forbidden
normal_final_rearm.precision_rule: Pass local_dtstart with YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS under the canonical timezone. Do not truncate or round seconds.
normal_final_rearm.exception_rule: Any delay other than +60 seconds on a normal CONTINUE close requires a fresh durable platform/safety/task constraint and an explicit exception_reason recorded with the run. Do not add extra local slack merely because scheduler delivery itself may be late.
normal_final_rearm.delivery_jitter_rule: Measure scheduled-due -> actual invocation separately. Do not hide provider delivery latency by lengthening the local completion-relative offset.

predictive_prearm_canary.reentry_condition: Do not repeat until UTIL-EXP-019 produces new evidence explaining or materially reducing successor observation/claim-to-first-useful delay.
predictive_prearm_canary.safety_rule: Any future retry still requires fresh authority fencing and no duplicate substantive side effects.

successor_start_measurement.rule: Do not infer missing boundaries. Attribute delay to the measured segment before changing scheduler timing again.
successor_start_measurement.latest_finding: STARTUP-006 was invoked 73s after due but left no durable BOOT_STARTED, REARM_VERIFIED, authority claim, useful work, or self-rearm. Hourly fallback recovered in STARTUP-007; fast independent wake remains unprovisioned.

evidence_basis.observed_sequence: Stage 1 woke, mutated the same canonical hourly RRULE DTSTART to actual wake +2m, persisted Stage 2 prompt, then Stage 2 executed and the same canary was disabled.

rollback: Preserve the canonical and completion-relative fallback whenever an experimental cadence produces unsafe overlap, missed continuation, rollback, or an out-of-budget useful-work handoff.

startup_acknowledgement.boot_started_semantics: Observed immediately after minimum fence validation proves bootstrap execution entered durable control handling.
startup_acknowledgement.rearm_verified_semantics: Observed only after the same canonical is enabled, recurring, and its provisional DTSTART is re-read successfully.
startup_acknowledgement.rule: Missing timestamps remain unknown. An invocation record alone does not prove bootstrap entry, rearm, authority, work, or process death.
startup_acknowledgement.recovery_limitation: This acknowledgement makes the failure diagnosable. It does not wake a worker; fast recovery still requires an independent supported trigger.
